- Can sponsors (we have two: LaunchLab and an ecosystem partner) both apply credits to the same Redwood account/project?
- How are promotional/onboarding credits shown on invoices versus committed reserved capacity?
- For the pilot, do you support splitting invoice lines (e.g., LaunchLab covers tokens 0–500k, partner covers 500k–1M) or do we need to create sub-accounts?

Hi Sara — great to hear from you. Short answer: yes, we can support sponsor credit stacking, but there are a few operational choices you’ll want to weigh. Below is a concise options matrix you can forward to finance. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Option A — Single Account, Credit Tiers (recommended for pilot)
- Mechanism: Create one Redwood project/account for the cohort. We apply credits from multiple sponsors sequentially by priority.
- Invoice view: Redwood shows invoice lines with consumption and then applies credit lines (e.g., Sponsor A credit: -$X, Sponsor B credit: -$Y, Promotional onboarding credit: -$Z).
- Pros: Simplest onboarding, single integration, less overhead for the cohort.
- Cons: Sponsor-level usage reporting is aggregated unless you include per-route tags.

Option B — Sub-accounts per Sponsor (preferred for long-term clarity)
- Mechanism: Create sub-accounts or separate API keys per sponsor. Each sponsor’s consumption invoices separately.
- Invoice view: Separate invoices/lines per sub-account; easier reconciliation for sponsors.
- Pros: Clear accounting for each sponsor; no ambiguity on who pays which tokens.
- Cons: Slightly more setup; cohort integration needs routing to the right key.

Notes on promotional/onboarding credits
- Promotional credits (Redwood or Redwood-provided promo) appear as a distinct credit line on the invoice and will be consumed after sponsor credits if you elect that ordering; ordering is configurable.
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) shows as a monthly committed line item; credits do not reduce committed capacity fees unless we agree a waiver in the contract.

Attachment: I’m attaching a proposed billing timeline spreadsheet and a one-page sample invoice that shows stacked credit lines.

Next steps: I’ll coordinate with Marissa on a pricing/packaging note and a short templated guide we can send to your finance team. Can you confirm whether LaunchLab prefers combined invoicing or separate sponsor invoices?

Cheers,
Ben

Hi Sara — looping in the pricing/ops perspective. Thanks for the MAAP; that helped. Wanted to share a policy + recommended packaging for cohorts like yours. Please find the short policy below you can paste into your internal note.

Redwood pilot sponsor-credit policy (recommended)- For short pilots (<90 days) we support credit stacking within one project. Sponsor credits are configured with a priority order; credits are consumed in priority unless parties request parallel allocation (requires sub-accounts).
- Promotional onboarding credit (Redwood) is applied last by default so sponsors see their committed value first; we can change ordering on request.
- For cohorts with multiple sponsors that require separate sponsor invoicing, we recommend creating per-sponsor API keys. Each key’s usage is invoiced separately to the sponsor email.
- Reserved capacity (dedicated GPU pools) is invoiced as a committed subscription and is not auto-offset by usage credits. Any waiver must be contractually agreed and is handled on a case-by-case basis.

Pricing/packaging suggestion for Founders Lab pilot- Pilot size: up to 1M tokens total over 8 weeks.
- Sponsor split (example): LaunchLab covers first 400k tokens; Ecosystem Partner covers next 400k; remaining 200k on promotional credits.
- Price cadence: usage billed at hosted API list price, credits applied as negative invoice lines; if you want unit-level discounts for sponsors we can offer a partner discount tier (5–15%) based on volume and logo placement.

I’ll prepare a one-page sample invoice and a short paragraph for your finance team to include in the MAAP. If LaunchLab confirms combined invoicing is OK, we’ll proceed with the single-account, priority-credit setup and provide exportable usage breakdowns by route so you can reconcile sponsor contributions.

Marissa
